title: What's your motivation to create your own game?
author: Post-reality
selftext:
As a young teen in the early-mid 2000's I got completely addicted and immersed by online game of that era. I assumed that as time goes on, online games would get even more difficult/competitive/challenging/immersive. Oh boy, I was so wrong. Instead of that, we got dumbed down mobile games with P2W and dailies.

  
I don't play games anymore as I feel like there are all too "casual" to my taste and not challenging enough. Definitely not immersive enough.

There's a certain type of game I fantasized about for more than 20 years already. I constantly nagged my software engineer younger brother to develop it for me, and I eventually even planned to hire developers or a game studio to develop it for me, however it was always scary to take that risk, as the game is pretty unique and complicated, and I was fearful of hitting a sunken cost fallacy, let alone the obvious risk of investment. The recent developments drastically changed the landscape. Now I'm able to develop it myself.

I don't want to share too many details, as I hate previewing and "early access". I would only show it once it's ready on release date (closed or open beta). No pre-Alpha or Alpha. But it's a hardcore online game with a pretty complicated action combat and a distinct, beautiful 2D art style (but the game itself could adhere to casuals as well as its scope is pretty big).

Hopefully in a year or so the game might be ready.



I would like to hear about your own stories :)

comments.author: glimsky
comments.body: Become a millionaire, buy fast cars and have bikini models on speed dial.

comments.author: svekkxor
comments.body:
I think most of us from that era share the same sentiment and need. 

For me, I found myself aimlessly wandering through my game library, while fantasising how cool gaming was before. There are some good indies though, but none really scratched that itch i had.

And now, with a strong software engineering background and the income to burn on tokens i finally found it is time to work on something of my own.

We'll see what time brings!

replies.author: Turbulent-Armadillo9
replies.body: I started about 8 months ago after wanting to make a game for about a decade. I’m now 8 months ahead if I had not started yet. Probably another year and a half for my project then my dream will have been fully realized :)

comments.author: JJBareaIsLeFather
comments.body: To build things I want to exist that don't.

replies.author: darkoblivion000
replies.body:
Yup exactly. I have ideas inside my head that I want to see realized and no one has done it well in the way I imagined. Will anyone else care? We’ll see I guess lol but I won’t stop until I have a product that represents what I imagined and is good enough for me. 

And if what’s good enough for me isn’t good enough for anyone else, then I guess I’m a little weird lol and that’s ok

replies.author: Turbulent-Armadillo9
replies.body: What a good attitude and a sick way to phrase it. From what I’ve seen around me, the people that make the best stuff are the ones who enjoy the process and are doing it to do it. It’s is fine to have other goals in mind too but putting this as priority number 1 is the way to go imho.

comments.author: Patient-Software-168
comments.body: Spiritual sequels to games that never got a sequel.

comments.author: Such--Balance
comments.body:
Tower defense game that is great.

With how easy this genre is in making the basic functionality, it seems its apperently very hard to transform that into an actual in depth amd balanced experience.

So i have set out to do just that. And with 'i' i mean my chatpgt and my codex

comments.author: Inner-Breath-4738
comments.body: Years ago I had a career break and learnt to write to a professional standard, not publishable though. Now i am preparing for early retirement and want to do it again, but this time using the game as the background and mechanism to tell a new story. It will take years but i will love every minute of building my own world.

comments.author: Ai_Test_4704
comments.body: I love the feel when I tell Claude; redesign the game from scratch, and he does it without asking why :)

comments.author: Tom_Baron
comments.body:
Too right on games getting dumbed down.

I was an avid gamer. In the same era you speak of, I loved strategy games, Mmorpgs, tycoon games and anything with a bit of thought behind it. More recently due to games not really catering for me, I learnt chess to a strong competitive club level.

Otb chess (real life tournament chess) is another level altogether. The emotion, the pressure and prolonged stress on your executive function is like no game out there.

So im colliding the world of multiplayer strategy games and otb chess. Real strategy though! Most strategy games actually just reward tactical play.

Players wont realise they are exposed to chess, the gameplay is strategy game 100%, but the cadence and mental load placed on the player is very similar to playing a game of classical chess otb.

The reason for doing all of this? I guess it hasnt been done before and i want to play it 😅
